authority: #K2-429 sec.3: why the channeled maze still fails on 3/5.
mechanism: the maze builds its grid over [min(pa,pb)-margin, max+margin] INTERSECT EDGE_IN INTERSECT WALL_RECT. With a tight per-row channel as WALL_RECT, the grid is the CHANNEL. The D1 endpoint-own-cell relaxation (R1156/R1158) deliberately refuses a cell OUTSIDE the wall (C35) - so if a net's reachable own-copper cell lies outside its channel, the maze reports no-free-start-node. That is exactly the observed blocked1 reason.
evidence: dry reading R1240: added 2 / blocked 3 with reasons no-free-start-node 1 and exhausted 2
the channel rects are the R1222 pad-laddered row corridors (2-3 mm wide)
R1158: the own-cell relaxation is explicitly wall-guarded (by design)
fix_direction: widen each net's channel to INCLUDE its reachable own-copper cell (deterministic: the channel = the row corridor UNION the endpoint-own-cell), or feed the channel as a SOFT preference plus a hard frame. Zero search; still deterministic.
next: apply the widen-and-include fix in the allocator, re-take the dry reading; then element-3; then a ruled N=1 application.
